proposals: DGCI&S should offer a bulk download of the full chapter-level export and import series for every fiscal year on TRADESTAT, so analysts are not forced to open a session and pull two fiscal years per query to build an eight-year history.

DGCI&S should mark each fiscal year’s figures in TRADESTAT as provisional or final, with the date of the last revision, so an endpoint such as FY2025-26 is not mistaken for a complete, settled year when growth rates are computed.

DGCI&S should publish quantity alongside value at chapter level for volatile chapters such as fertilisers and mineral fuels, so it is possible to tell how much of a spike or collapse is price and how much is volume.

The Department of Commerce should show the annual series or the peak year beside any multi-year growth rate it cites for a trade chapter in official releases, so round trips like iron and steel exports are not presented as steady growth.
